beforeImage.name: Natural Gas Pipeline Co. of America
beforeImage.description: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America is a large interstate natural gas transmission and storage system. The asset serves producers, utilities, marketers, and industrial users through an asset-heavy, predominantly fee-based transportation and storage model. ArcLight stated in 2025 that NGPL includes about 9,100 miles of pipeline, more than one million horsepower of compression, and approximately 288 Bcf of working gas storage. The scale of the system makes it one of the larger gas infrastructure platforms in North America. ArcLight announced in May 2025 that, after acquiring Brookfield's remaining 25% interest, it would become NGPL's largest owner with a 62.5% economic interest alongside operator Kinder Morgan's 37.5% interest.

Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America (NGPL)
afterImage.description: Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC (NGPL) is a major U.S. interstate natural-gas transmission and storage company serving producers, utilities, marketers, power generators, industrial users and LNG-linked markets. Kinder Morgan's audited 2025 reporting lists approximately 9,105 miles of pipeline, 8.40 Bcf/d of design capacity and 288 Bcf of storage capacity. The network spans nine states and connects major U.S. supply basins with Midwest demand centers and Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast markets. NGPL provides firm, flexible-firm and interruptible transportation, multiple storage products, balancing, park-and-loan and line-pack services. ArcLight-controlled funds own 62.5%, across separate Fund VII and Fund VIII investments, while Kinder Morgan owns 37.5% and operates the system. Brookfield fully exited in May 2025, and no later NGPL-specific sale or pending ownership change was identified through August 13, 2026.
